title: Local magnetic resonance of scalar spin chirality
abstract: Quantum states with finite scalar spin chirality carry an orbital magnetic moment that has so far eluded direct measurement. We show that, whereas uniform electron spin resonance preserves chirality, a local drive breaks the cyclic symmetry and activates chirality-changing transitions, providing direct access to the chiral orbital magnetic moment. Lindblad simulations demonstrate experimentally accessible signatures in platforms with local spin addressability, including electron spin resonance with a scanning tunneling microscope, donor spins in silicon, and quantum-dot spin qubits.
summary: This paper proposes using local magnetic resonance techniques to directly measure the orbital magnetic moment associated with scalar spin chirality in quantum magnetic systems. By applying a local drive that breaks rotational symmetry, the authors predict distinct spectroscopic signatures—such as peak splittings or homodyne resonance features—that allow for the quantitative determination of this elusive chiral moment.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of directly measuring the orbital magnetic moment associated with scalar spin chirality (SSC), a property that is difficult to probe experimentally.
main_result: Local magnetic resonance, achieved by breaking the system's rotational symmetry with a local drive, provides a spectroscopic route to measure this chiral orbital magnetic moment.
method: The authors propose and simulate two protocols: direct chirality resonance via homodyne detection, and chirality-resolved spin resonance by observing peak splittings in ESR measurements.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using an antiferromagnetic spin trimer or, more generally, a Hubbard model on a triangular ring subjected to a magnetic flux. The dynamics are governed by the Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: The primary observables are the chiral orbital magnetic moment ($\mu_\chi$), the resonance signal $\Delta I_{hom}$ in homodyne detection, and the splitting ($\delta\chi$) of spin resonance peaks.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the coupling strength ($\lambda$), the magnetic field ($B$), and the ratio of relaxation rates ($r = T_{1,\chi}/T_{1,s}$).
main_assumptions: The method critically relies on the local drive breaking the $C_3$ rotational symmetry, and simulations assume regimes where $k_B T$ is small compared to energy splittings.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows energy level splitting due to chirality. Figure 2 illustrates the homodyne signal $\Delta I_{hom}$ vs. detuning, showing resonant features. Figure 3 simulates ESR-STM resonance, confirming peaks at $\Delta_z \pm \delta\chi$. Figure 4 analyzes the resolution of the chiral splitting.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework linking SSC to an orbital moment. It then details the two spectroscopic protocols (homodyne detection and spin resonance) using the Lindblad master equation to model the time evolution and measurable signals.
why_interesting: This work bridges fundamental concepts of quantum magnetism (chirality) with advanced experimental techniques (STM, quantum dots), providing a concrete, measurable signature for a subtle quantum property.
